name: Miro
look: Stark white canvas, canary-yellow wordmark, black pill CTAs, pastel sticky-note feature cards and a massive dark footer.

hero.title: Where teams actually think together
hero.sub: An infinite canvas for workshops, diagrams, planning and the messy middle of any project. Sixty million people use one, mostly because the alternative is a photograph of a whiteboard.

features.title: One canvas, all the messy bits
features.sub: The parts of the work that never fit in a document or a ticket.

items.title: Sticky notes
items.body: The obvious one, done properly — bulk create, cluster by colour, and convert a cluster into a list when the workshop ends.

items.title: Diagrams
items.body: Flowcharts, architecture and sequence diagrams with connectors that stay attached when you move the box.

items.title: Live collaboration
items.body: Cursors, follow-me presenting, and a timer that everyone can see. Up to three hundred people on one board.

items.title: Workshop tools
items.body: Voting, timers and private mode, so a workshop can run without a separate facilitation stack.

items.title: Templates
items.body: Two and a half thousand of them — retros, story maps, service blueprints — most contributed by users.

items.title: Integrations
items.body: Two-way sync with your tracker, so a sticky note becomes a ticket and the ticket's status comes back to the board.

showcases.title: Facilitation without a second toolkit
showcases.body: Timers, dot voting, private mode and follow-me presenting are on the board itself. You stop switching between a whiteboard, a timer app and a poll, and the workshop stops stalling every time you do.
points: Private mode so nobody anchors on the first idea

showcases.title: Sticky notes that become tickets
showcases.body: Two-way sync with your tracker. Convert a cluster into issues, and status changes flow back onto the board so the retro board does not quietly go stale the week after the retro.
points: Convert clusters to issues in bulk
Status syncs back onto the card
Jira, Linear, Asana and Azure Boards

gallery.title: Templates
gallery.sub: Two and a half thousand, most of them contributed by the people who use them.

testimonial.quote: We ran a three-day workshop across four time zones on one board. The board is still open eight months later and people still add to it, which is not something a whiteboard photo has ever done.
testimonial.name: Nadia Haddad

pricing.title: Plans for every team
pricing.sub: Free forever for three boards. Paid plans unlock unlimited boards and admin controls.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.desc: For trying it and small projects.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.desc: Unlimited boards for a small team.

items.q: Is the free plan really free?
items.a: Yes, permanently, with three editable boards and unlimited collaborators on them. Older boards become view-only rather than being deleted if you go over.

items.q: How many people can be on one board?
items.a: Three hundred concurrent editors. Beyond about fifty, follow-me presenting and private mode are what keep it usable rather than chaotic.
As PDF, image, or CSV of the notes and their groupings. Boards can also be backed up in bulk from the admin console on Business.
Partially. Recently opened boards are cached and edits queue locally, syncing when you reconnect. Creating a new board needs a connection.

cta.title: Open a board and see
cta.sub: Free forever for three boards. No card, and your team can join without an account.

footer.tagline: An infinite canvas for the parts of the work that never fit in a document.

notes: A stark white canvas with the wordmark in canary yellow is the opening signature. The yellow is brand, not a UI accent.
Black pills are the dominant interactive element — the primary CTA is black, never yellow.
Feature cards draw from the actual sticky-note palette: yellow, rose, coral, teal and mint.
Real board mockups are the feature imagery. Abstract illustration would undercut the whole premise.
The footer is a massive dark band with multi-column links — the one heavy surface in an otherwise white system.
